title: Fix it: turn a list of http headers into a lookup object
basics: A key in parentheses is computed from an expression: `{ (k): v }` uses the value of `k` as the field name. Wrapping an Array of objects in `{( )}` merges them into one object: `{ ([{a: 1}, {b: 2}]) }` is `{ a: 1, b: 2 }`.
prompt:
The script in the editor is **almost** right. It passes on the sample and fails on a case you cannot see.

The original task was:

An API gateway logs request headers as an array of `{ name, value }`. Downstream code wants a single object keyed by header name, so it can read `headers."content-type"`.

HTTP header names are case-insensitive, and different clients send `Content-Type` or `content-type`. Use the lower-case name as the key.

Find what is wrong and fix it. You can press Run to see what it currently does.
hints: Run it on the sample first. If the sample looks right, the bug only shows on data the sample does not contain.
Ask what kind of input would break this — an empty list, a missing field, a value ordered differently.
keeps the name as sent, so Content-Type and content-type are different keys

explanation.approach: A computed key needs parentheses, and the list of one-field objects that `map` produces has to be merged with `{( )}`. Lower-casing the name makes the key predictable no matter how the client spelled it.

snippets.label: One object per header
snippets.note: An Array, not a lookup object.
